title: Minato’s and Yori’s relationship in Kore-Eda’s Monster/Kaibutsu (2023)

commenti.body:
I didn't catch the fire/water thing, but it's a very densely-written movie. You might be onto something. 

I saw it twice. On the second viewing, it became clear how carefully-written the script is. Every detail is crucial.

Also, I tried not to cry the 2nd time...but, I failed. Incredible film.

Amazing that you picked up on this detail!!! I did find an article where Kore-eda confirmed he did indeed think about the relationship between fire and water when making the film. It's not coincidental the >!film started with a fire (and there's this association between it and Yori) and ended with a storm!<. And the >!cat burial scene cements this motif/theme!<, just like you said, and is also a gentle >!foreshadowing!< of the ending. I can't remember where I read the article or whether it was in English or Japanese (I'm positive it's the former tho). Let me try to find it, and if I do I'll post it here for you and everyone to read. My interpretation of >!Yori/Minato's relationship!< and the >!fire/water dynamic between them!< is that >!fire represents the children's early thinking, that there's something wrong with them that needs to be fixed (they need to be reborn, so does the cat). However, the burning of the cat was stopped half way through by Minato with water!<. This foreshadows >!a shift in their mentality, which we see later on. Water is the cleansing and removal of barriers (judgments, prejudices, anything stopping individuals from being themselves) in society. It's the rebirth of society, and not of the children themselves. Thus in the ending scene, the kids realized they stayed the same, it's the world, now free of barriers, of obstacles standing in their way of being true to themselves (the gate blocking the train tracks seen earlier in the film) thanks to the storm, that has been reborn for them!<

And hey, I also think it's the best movie I've ever seen. I used to not have a favorite movie (I always said one of my favorites hehe), but Monster's changed that for me. I think (and hope) that it will stay my favorite film forever :)

thanks a lot for clearing that up!! I’ll be waiting for an article if that won’t be too hard to find again :)

I do get the ending with a storm before their >! rebirth into the world with no barriers !< and i thought that storm itself was symbolising >! Minato’s/Yori’s feelings and worryings + if we are talking about it from Saori’s pov it’s her and Hori sensei’s messes in their heads that they actually made Minato in the first place and Yori hurt I think !< . i fully agree with u + i think many people have different feelings about each detail, maybe some even didn’t pay that much attention to it, but it’s that movie that most people will be calling a masterpiece no matter what (and that’s definitely true :) )
It may take me a few weeks but I'll try to find it, since I want to share all the results of my research on the film with like-minded people and exchange views with them, too :D

well, each person pays attention to  different details of Kaibutsu and each person gets different associations when it not only comes to Minato and Yori/their relationship, but the whole movie itself too. 

woaaah, im glad u have a chance to see it two times, it was my first as u can tell and i still got so emotional over this breathtaking masterpiece:)

u’re so real for that!! I’m also not the type of person to have something favourite in general (songs/movies/books/etc), but Monster truly got my heart, i think every person that faced at least one of various problems in this film will like it forever will their whole heart.
woah, that’s impressive :o gl on that!! I’m sure u’ll find it!!
hehe drag someone to the theatre and make them watch this movie. we don't deserve >!to cry alone, make other people experience our heartache too!< :)))
was with friends/family both times. There's something about the pacing and the music of this film -- it's conducive to looong stretches of tears.

Your analysis of water/fire dynamics in the relationship expressed visually through their clothing choices is fantastic! It's what makes the beauty of film analysis so delightful - you've made an observation that totally makes sense within the context but it wasn't directly addressed by Kore-Eda (at least not as far as I've seen in his interviews). It would be super cool if that's what he was hinting at, but until he confirms it or provides his own perspective, it's open to an individual's interpretation like yours. I totally see your point though! The contrast, conflict, and duality embedded in water/fire symbolisms might echo the complexities of their relationship perfectly! And as always, Kore-Eda is a genius in expressing human emotions and relationships vividly on screen.

thank u a lot!! i think many details in the film are quite obvious, but u start to notice them only after rewatching/rethinking each scene.

some cool person here replied and actually said that they saw info that Kore-Eda used some fire/water dynamics in the film, but they’re not sure if it is fully true, so we’ll just wait until that cool user will try to find that article again!! (really hope that they will eventually)

and I fully agree that Kore-Eda is a true genius that definitely knows how to make the audience feel all kinds of emotions watching just one movie!

Gosh, I found it!!! [https://mksports.co.kr/view/2023/766394](https://mksports.co.kr/view/2023/766394)

Okay so this article is in Korean lol, so you're going to have to use google translate/ask someone who speaks Korean to help. And I think it's based on the press conference + stage greeting/stage interview that Kore-eda did with the child actors Kurokawa Soya and Hiiragi Hinata at Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) back in Nov/early December. If like me you dig the interactions/chemistry of the child actors, here's the full video of the event: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R\_jbnv0-ex4&t=1s](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R_jbnv0-ex4&t=1s). I'm sure the article I actually read was a different one, since I remember seeing it back in October, way before BIFF. Like I said if I ever come across it again I'll share it. But I hope the links I provided above are enough to confirm your interpretation :)))

I've been watching many interviews of Kurokawa (who played Minato) and Hiiragi (who played Yori), simply because their real-life goofiness >!makes the movie a lot less heartbreaking!<. The kids are really goofy and funny (but also smart and quite mature) hehe. 

Also, my Japanese sucks, and I've forgotten most what I learned 5-6 years ago, and this is all just my silly fan theory, but if you look at the real names of the actors, and think about the water/fire dynamic, somehow they're really born to play these roles. Kurokawa means black (kuro) river (kawa). And somehow when watching the film I associated Minato very closely with night (black/dark) and water (river). Whereas Hiiragi means a holy tree, and Hinata means the sun (heat, fire, daytime, which the character of Yori could be said to represent lol). When in Cannes, Hiiragi even told people to call him Sunny since many people could not pronounce his Japanese name Hinata :))) That kid's really quick-witted (and extremely good at fan-service) hehe.

So true!!! The music is such a highlight of the film. I teared up a bit >!when Hwit was played in the first act (the my brain was switched with that of a pig scene)!<, then when I heard >!Monster 2 at the end of the second act!<. In the third act, it's >!20220302 and Aqua that got me!<. Damn! Agree with you about the pacing and structure of the film. Lots of people who complained about the film being too slow or the third act being too short and not coming soon enough to save the day kinda...missed the point I think. And it's alright, maybe the movie is just not for them. The impact of the third act wouldn't have been so great had the movie not been structured and paced the way it was, with >!the first and second acts being laborious and intense. And that's an intentional choice to juxtapose the adult world in the movie with the innocent world of the children, where things feel really easy, relaxed, and endlessly lovely!<

omg, im forever thankful to u for finding that one, even if it’s not the exact same one!! i’ll ask my korean friend to help me with translation for sure, cause i really don’t know any korean:D but once again thank u so so so much for it!!

 i had been following both of them since March of this year (around time of first big announcements about Kaibutsu release) and they’re really the definition of silliness irl, i agree!

i adore how much u go into details even about the meaning of their names drawing a line to the actual meaning of characters names in the film, seriously, an amazing theory and also, I’ll add something to ur theory, which isn’t exactly the smartest thought - Soya 想矢 is like a thoughtful person, but another variations of the name are 蒼也, so 蒼 is basically blue as a colour and there’s also 
蒼夜 in which so 蒼 - is once again blue colour (water association is the first thing that pops up in my head),ya夜 - similar to Minato’s which means night. once again, not the smartest theory, but i tried to connect it with his role of Minato as close as possible :)

Oh yeah I've been thinking a lot about how the Soya part of his name should be understood as it's not as straightforward as Hinata. Like it's something like being thoughtful/thinking right but also the last Kanji character is the kanji for an arrow as well, so...I kinda lost it there :))) Thanks for adding to my silly fan theory hahaha. The connection is lovely. And Minato actually means port, so there you go, another water association. Whereas Hoshikawa (Yori's last name) means something like a river of stars (again, heat, light, brightness, fire). Anyway, I think "thoughtfulness" is something that fits well with both the real-life Kurokawa and Kurokawa as Minato. Both are gentle, sensitive, and really really caring and thoughtful towards others (especially real-life Hiiragi who's also younger in age). Real-life Hiiragi on the other hand is just really really Yori, he's bright, talkative, cheerful, and very very mischevious, always teasing Kurokawa. But he's also somewhat more aloof with his head in the clouds and isn't the type who fits in well with children his age :)))

yeaaa, 矢 kinda made me lost too, so I had to go with different variation of Soya :D 

i guess they were really made for this roles, i love how cute their interactions are too from what i saw! their connection is full of cuteness:)
